newsitem.title: CHINA: Greenspan ends China trip, boosts central bank ties.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan ends China trip, boosts central bank ties.

text.p: U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan wound up a visit to China on Friday aimed at strengthening ties between the central banks of the two countries.

During his three-day stay, Greenspan exchanged views with senior Chinese officials and economists on financial and central bank issues in the United States and China, according to a prepared statement released on his departure.

Greenspan met Chinese President Jiang Zemin as well as Vice- Premier and economic tsar Zhu Rongji, People's Bank of China (central bank) Governor Dai Xianglong, Finance Minister Liu Zhongli and State Planning Commission chief Chen Jinhua.
China has been trying to strengthen its central bank by giving it more independence and expanding its ability to supervise the banking system.

Beijing has sought help from foreign central banks to boost the role of market mechanisms to control money supply instead of relying on administrative measures favoured in the days of economic central planning.
The statement said Greenspan's visit was part of an ongoing process of cooperation between the central banks of the two countries.
